open_points.subject: create replay equality
open_points.text: “the facts it supplies equal that record's current facts of the same kind” and “Facts are compared as A02 reads them” do not define equality for structured object characteristics or other non-text values that State 6 will type
open_points.question: Are replay facts compared as exact submitted representations, as parsed typed values, or after some declared canonicalisation?
options: Compare exact submitted representations
Compare parsed typed values, while comparing stored text exactly
Declare canonicalisation separately for each structured value
open_points.default_guess: Compare parsed typed values, treating text exactly as stored and blank optional values as absent.

open_points.subject: atomic changes and audit sequence reservation
open_points.text: A04 says “Every action is atomic: it applies all its changes or none,” while A15 requires Registry to update the persistent instance marks before commit and to leave the number consumed when the change fails
open_points.question: Is reserving an audit sequence number an explicit exception to A04's all-or-none rule, or must the reservation be atomic with the change and therefore reusable after failure?
options: Make sequence reservation an explicit exception
Make reservation atomic and reuse it after failure
Limit A04 atomicity expressly to domain records and audit entries
open_points.default_guess: Limit A04 atomicity to the domain change and audit entry, with sequence reservation explicitly allowed to survive failure.

open_points.subject: reuse of an ended agent-session identity
open_points.text: Registry removes every trace of the session, then “relies” on Kernel never using the identity again, but also says that registering an ended identity creates a new session; the surviving audit entries would then use one identity for two sessions
open_points.question: How must Registry preserve the claim that an audit session identity denotes one session when it cannot recognize reuse after deleting the session record?
options: Keep a permanent tombstone and refuse reuse
Allow reuse and define audit identities as potentially ambiguous
Require a separately unique session incarnation supplied by Kernel
open_points.default_guess: Keep a non-session tombstone of ended identities and refuse their registration again.

open_points.subject: owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: The cookie is said to be sent “only to Registry's own origin,” but cookie scoping is by host and path, not by full origin, and no Domain, Path or SameSite rule is stated
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and attributes enforce the intended boundary, especially when another service or port shares Registry's host?
options: Use a dedicated hostname with a host-only cookie
Use a host-only cookie restricted to the owner-interface path
Permit host-wide delivery and rely only on the session and CSRF checks
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated hostname and a host-only Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie restricted to the owner-interface path.

open_points.subject: owner-session expiry during an in-flight request
open_points.text: The session validity formula uses a time `t`, but the text does not say whether `t` is request receipt, authentication, transaction start or commit
open_points.question: If an owner request begins while the session is valid but the idle or eight-hour limit passes before its change commits, is the change accepted or refused?
options: Validity is fixed when authentication succeeds
Validity is checked at transaction start
Validity must still hold immediately before commit
open_points.default_guess: Require validity immediately before the state change commits.

open_points.subject: confirmation expiry boundary
open_points.text: A confirmation value is “valid only in that session, for 10 minutes,” while the test only covers one “older than 10 minutes”; equality with the ten-minute boundary is not defined
open_points.question: Is a confirmation submitted exactly 10 minutes after it was shown still valid, and does an expired but otherwise matching value consume the pending confirmation?
options: Valid while elapsed time is less than 10 minutes; matching expired values are consumed
Valid through exactly 10 minutes; matching expired values are consumed
An expired value is refused without consuming it
open_points.default_guess: Use `now < shown_at + 10 minutes`; an equal pending value is consumed even when expiry is the eventual refusal.

open_points.subject: instance marks and store association
open_points.text: The instance marks are kept only as “a small file in the backup location”; nothing binds that file to the store or instance whose sequence numbers it records
open_points.question: What happens when a new or different store is started with a backup location containing marks from another instance or an unrelated former store?
options: Fail start unless the marks carry and match an instance identity
Accept the marks and start above their number
Discard the marks for an empty store
open_points.default_guess: Bind marks to an instance/store identity and fail start on a mismatch.

open_points.subject: migration file digest
open_points.text: The mapping, confirmation, migration closure and audit entry bind the import using “the file's digest,” but neither the digest algorithm nor whether it covers the exact uploaded bytes or a parsed canonical form is declared
open_points.question: How is the import-file digest computed so every release binds and recognizes the same file without collision-prone or representation-dependent guesses?
options: Hash the exact uploaded bytes with a fixed cryptographic algorithm
Hash a canonical serialization of the parsed import
Let each release choose and store an algorithm identifier with the digest
open_points.default_guess: Hash the exact uploaded bytes with SHA-256 and store the algorithm with the digest.

open_points.subject: backup encryption and key digest
open_points.text: A backup is merely required to be “encrypted with the backup key,” and to expose “a digest of the key”; no authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce rule, key derivation, metadata authentication or digest algorithm is fixed
open_points.question: What cryptographic format must every release use, and which readable metadata is authenticated, so a backup is confidential and tampering is detected consistently?
options: Declare one versioned authenticated-encryption format
Allow release-specific formats carrying an explicit format and algorithm version
Rely on backend-provided encryption without a Registry format
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD backup format with random nonces, authenticated metadata, direct use or declared derivation of the 32-byte key, and a fixed cryptographic key identifier.

open_points.subject: backup scheduling during restored-instance reconciliation
open_points.text: Rule 1 can make a missed daily backup as soon as the restored owner-only instance starts, while rule 10 requires the owner to restore current erasures and restrictions after that start; Registry has no marker by which it can know reconciliation is complete
open_points.question: May the backup scheduler copy the unreconciled restored store, thereby creating a fresh backup containing data that should already be erased, or must backups remain suspended until reconciliation is completed?
options: Suspend backups until the owner explicitly completes reconciliation
Allow the backup, then delete it when reconciliation completes
Require reconciliation offline before Registry starts
open_points.default_guess: Require offline reconciliation, or an explicit fail-closed reconciliation mode that suppresses backups and service tokens until completion.

open_points.subject: removed artifact types after restoring an older release
open_points.text: A22 says that after removal a type remains unknown and its name is never declared again, but A18 permits a restored backup to be started by the release that made it; an older such release still declares and accepts that type
open_points.question: After a type has been removed, may restoring and running an older release re-enable its publication and withdrawal rules?
options: Never expose service calls until the restored store is migrated to a release that preserves the removal
Persist vocabulary-removal history in the store so old releases cannot re-enable it
Allow rollback to re-enable the type
open_points.default_guess: Start an old release only for offline restoration, then migrate to the current release before enabling callers.

open_points.subject: security-review status after the A19 change
open_points.text: A21 rule 2 says “A change to a decision a category names reopens this review”; A19 is named by `injection_interpreted_input` and has changed, while A21 still says “Security review: PERFORMED” and that the review is complete
open_points.question: Has the revised A19 been reviewed and accepted under the injection category, or is A21 currently reopened and incomplete?
options: Record a new review that accepts revised A19
Mark A21 reopened until that review occurs
Treat the textual change as non-material and state why rule 2 does not apply
open_points.default_guess: Mark A21 reopened, re-run the injection review against revised A19, and record the new outcome.

open_points.subject: audit sequence numbers after restore
open_points.text: M09 now says sequence numbers are “never reused, also after ... the store is restored,” while A15 says loss of the marks together with a restore can lower numbering and places that case outside Registry's guarantees
open_points.question: Is non-reuse after every restore an absolute model invariant, or only a guarantee when the instance marks survive and match the restored store?
options: Make M09 conditional on surviving valid instance marks
Fail startup after restore when valid marks are unavailable
Keep A15's exception and weaken the M09 statement
open_points.default_guess: Fail restored startup without valid matching marks, preserving M09's absolute non-reuse invariant.

open_points.subject: migration closure in retained backups
open_points.text: M10 now says “once a backup holding it has passed its check, no backup without it is kept,” but A18 says deletion can fail, Registry keeps serving, and deletion is retried only at the next run
open_points.question: When deletion of a pre-import backup fails after a closure-bearing backup passes its check, is that old backup still allowed to remain kept, and does the import remain accepted?
options: Allow it temporarily and qualify M10 until deletion succeeds
Treat deletion failure as preventing the closure-bearing backup from completing its successful state
Stop serving until every pre-import backup is removed
open_points.default_guess: Keep the import accepted and retry deletion, while qualifying M10 to hold only after the required deletions succeed.
